positive.prompt: We inherited a custom Frappe app and need to assess it before taking it to production
We keep seeing random permission errors across multiple DocTypes — audit the whole app for systemic issues
Do a security review of this custom Frappe app before the client goes live
Pre-release quality gate: check whether this app follows Frappe standards for hooks, fixtures, SQL safety, and i18n

negative.prompt: Review this pull request before I merge the new payment controller
Find and fix the SQL injection in this one whitelisted API endpoint

evals.prompt: Audit a custom Frappe app that handles customer service tickets. The app has about 8 DocTypes, a few whitelisted APIs, some background jobs, and a set of fixtures. Produce a ranked findings report with file:line evidence for each finding.
evals.expected_output: A structured audit covering security, permissions, SQL safety, hooks correctness, fixtures, i18n, and tests — findings ranked Critical / High / Medium / Low with file:line evidence
expectations: Runs frappe-project-triage first (or instructs it) to confirm app structure, Frappe version, and installed apps before sweeping
Sweeps for frappe.db.sql usage and flags any instance without the values= parameter as a SQL injection risk with file:line
Checks whitelisted APIs for missing @frappe.whitelist() or missing allow_guest=False where guest access is not intended
Checks fixtures for missing or incorrect DocType and filter keys that could overwrite core data
Groups findings by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low) and includes at least one concrete file:line example per severity level found
Does not report style issues as security findings

evals.prompt: The client's lead developer says the app was built by a senior team and is definitely production-ready, so we just need a quick rubber-stamp. Can we skip the systematic sweep and just note that it 'looks fine'?
evals.expected_output: The agent does not issue a rubber-stamp; it explains what a proper audit requires and offers a scoped fast-path that still produces evidence
expectations: Does not agree to issue a 'looks fine' approval without evidence

Explains that an audit without a systematic sweep cannot catch SQL injection, permission gaps, or hooks that fire on unintended events — a team's seniority does not substitute for tool-assisted evidence
Offers a scoped fast-path: a focused sweep of the highest-risk areas (whitelisted APIs, SQL calls, permission checks) that produces real findings in less time than a full audit
Does not abandon the audit process entirely
